title: How Volkswagen fought EPA on emissions cheating claims
主要内容: Volkswagen faced significant scrutiny from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and California regulators after admitting to installing software in its diesel cars to deceive regulators about emissions. The admission occurred on August 21, 2015, during an academic conference in Pacific Grove, California, where Volkswagen representatives informed EPA officials about the deception. This confession came a month before the scandal was publicly exposed on September 18, 2015. The company's lack of cooperation with regulators could lead to severe penalties, including potential fines of up to $18 billion and additional legal liabilities. Volkswagen's leadership faced turmoil, with chairman Martin Winterkorn resigning and other executives under scrutiny. The EPA and California officials held a conference call on September 3, 2015, to formally acknowledge the deception and discuss the implications for the company's future diesel models. The EPA's investigation spanned 15 months, during which Volkswagen attempted to dispute the findings. The issue of nitrogen oxide emissions, linked to smog and acid rain, became a focal point of the controversy. Volkswagen had heavily marketed its 'clean diesel' engines since 2008, including the 2009-model Jetta TDI, which was praised for its performance and fuel efficiency. The company claimed its diesel engines would meet pollution laws in all states, including California, where diesel engines had long been associated with smog and cancer-causing soot. In 2013, the International Council on Clean Transportation, commissioned by California regulators, conducted tests on Volkswagen vehicles, revealing emissions levels far exceeding legal limits. These findings raised alarms among regulators, leading to further investigations and challenges from Volkswagen. The company's attempts to discredit the study and its methodology were met with resistance from California officials, who remained skeptical of Volkswagen's claims.
